binders: Universally quantify m over all natural numbers, including zero.
For each m, universally quantify q: ℝ × ℝ → ℝ^m, represented as q(x,t)(i) for i∈Fin m.
Universally quantify flux: ℝ^m → ℝ^m. It depends on the entire state vector and has no separate spatial or temporal argument.
In spatial integrability, a, b, and t range independently over ℝ.
In temporal flux integrability, x, s, and t range independently over ℝ.
In the balance identity, a, b, s, and t range independently over ℝ.
In the derivative clause, a and b are universally quantified first, followed by almost every real t. The variable s inside the differentiated function is a bound time argument.
hypotheses: There are no separate assumptions on q or flux outside the equivalence.
The left-hand property consists of conditions A, B, and C defined below.
conclusions: For every m, q, and flux, (A ∧ B ∧ C) if and only if (A ∧ B ∧ C ∧ D).
A: For every a,b,t∈ℝ, the function x↦q(x,t) is μ-integrable on both (a,b] and (b,a].
B: For every x,s,t∈ℝ, the function τ↦flux(q(x,τ)) is μ-integrable on both (s,t] and (t,s].
C: For every a,b,s,t∈ℝ, ∫_a^b q(x,t) dμ(x) − ∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x) = ∫_s^t [flux(q(a,τ)) − flux(q(b,τ))] dμ(τ), as an equality in ℝ^m.
D: For every a,b∈ℝ, for μ-almost every t∈ℝ, the function s↦∫_a^b q(x,s) dμ(x) has ordinary real derivative flux(q(a,t)) − flux(q(b,t)) at t.
mathematical_definitions: μ denotes the distinguished measure Real.measureSpace.volume used in the supplied declaration.
ℝ^m is the finite function space Fin m → ℝ with coordinatewise addition, subtraction, and real scalar multiplication, its finite product normed-space structure, and its product topology.
For a vector-valued function f, ∫_a^b f dμ means ∫_(a,b] f dμ − ∫_(b,a] f dμ, using vector-valued measure integrals.
Interval integrability is the conjunction of integrability on these two half-open intervals; it imposes no ordering on the endpoints.
Writing M_ab(u)=∫_a^b q(x,u) dμ(x), the derivative assertion is M_ab(t+h)−M_ab(t)−h[flux(q(a,t))−flux(q(b,t))]=o(|h|) in the vector topology as h→0.
For each fixed a,b, almost everywhere means the set of times where the stated derivative property fails has μ-measure zero.
LocalDef001(q,flux) is exactly A ∧ B ∧ C, with no additional hidden condition in its supplied definition.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any finite number of real state coordinates, any state function q of a real spatial variable and a real time variable, and any state-to-flux map, the following balance property is equivalent to the same property together with an almost-everywhere time derivative formula. The balance property requires spatial integrability of q between every pair of finite spatial endpoints at every time, temporal integrability of the flux at every fixed spatial point between every pair of finite times, and equality between the change in the spatial integral and the temporal integral of left endpoint flux minus right endpoint flux. The additional formula says that, for each fixed pair of spatial endpoints, the spatial integral has time derivative equal to that same boundary flux difference for almost every time. All integrals and exceptional sets use the dossier's distinguished real volume measure μ. The substantive implication is that the three balance conditions imply this additional derivative formula; the reverse implication retains those three conditions.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension m need not be positive. For m=0, the state space has a single empty vector, so the vector identities and derivative assertion are trivial and integrability is that of the zero vector.
Both independent variables range over all of ℝ. No restriction to nonnegative time, a bounded spatial domain, or a prescribed time interval is encoded.
All interval endpoints are finite real numbers, with no assumptions a≤b or s≤t. Integrals are oriented.
For a=b the spatial integral and boundary flux difference are zero, so that instance of the balance and derivative clauses is trivial. For s=t the balance identity is also trivial.

The exceptional null set in the derivative clause may depend on a and b, as well as on the fixed q and flux. A single common full-measure set valid for all real endpoint pairs is not explicitly required.

There are no existential state or flux witnesses: both functions are arbitrary universally quantified inputs. If exceptional null sets are introduced in an English reformulation, they are chosen after the spatial endpoints.
The derivative is asserted for the spatial integral of q, not for q itself. No pointwise differential equation involving spatial or temporal derivatives of q is explicitly asserted.
No continuity, differentiability, or global measurability assumption on flux is imposed. Only the indicated temporal compositions must satisfy the stated interval integrability.

Spatial integrability is required at every time and temporal flux integrability at every spatial point, not merely at almost every slice. No separate joint space-time integrability hypothesis is present.
No initial condition, boundary condition, entropy condition, uniqueness statement, or existence statement for solutions is encoded.
The first three conditions remain on the right of the equivalence. The proposition does not claim that the almost-everywhere derivative formula alone implies the integrated balance property.

Although measure integrals are total operations in Lean, the integrability clauses accompany every relevant spatial integral and each boundary flux trace, preventing a balance assertion based solely on values assigned to nonintegrable integrands.
ambiguities: D065 exposes Real.measureSpace only as inferInstance. The packet does not reveal which measure-space instance is selected or its normalization. The translation therefore retains μ=Real.measureSpace.volume explicitly; identifying μ as standard Lebesgue measure requires an additional semantic expansion.

The finite product norm in D051 and D052 is inherited from the unexpanded Pi.seminormedAddGroup. Its precise numerical formula is not supplied. The translation uses the displayed finite product normed structure and product topology without asserting a particular norm formula.
